ops.body: INTERIM WORKAROUND EXISTS, reviewed and field-staged (2026-07-26): a standalone bbolt tool (dkservicefix) that dumps the store (flagging session-keyed records and the replacement bucket's fence state) and repairs it by deleting BOTH the desired and applied records for every keyed label — Option B from the surgery spec, chosen because deleting only the desired record makes the next open's reconcile treat applied-without-desired as removal and bootout + os.Remove the working plist. Source preserved as an attachment on incident timeline log 68c576df (the /tmp working copies rot in ~3 days); rebuild: standalone module, go.etcd.io/bbolt v1.5.0, CGO_ENABLED=0. Procedure: cp -p backup → dump (verify expected state, stop on drift) → fix → re-dump (zero keyed) → the consumer's install runs clean and Converge supersedes with the fresh agent set. Preconditions built into the tool: regular file mode 0600, absolute path required, 3s flock timeout (serve never holds the store lock — only install/uninstall do). Known nuance: a record failing JSON decode reads as unkeyed and is skipped by fix (deliberate — never delete what can't be reasoned about); dump surfaces it loudly as DECODE ERROR. This tool becomes obsolete once the drift-arm fix (this task's proper resolution, in the v0.20.9 bundle) is deployed fleet-wide.
